key_highlights: ASX posts fourth consecutive losing week as rising bond yields pressure equities; broad-based sell-off across sectors
RBA signals continued hikes despite surging unemployment, trapping borrowers in an interest-rate pincer
AUD experiences sharp depreciation ('trapdoor'), amplifying import costs and pressure on resource exporters
Australian house prices over halfway through largest 40-year correction, with Victoria hit hardest
Unemployment surges, with more than half of renters financially stressed; Victoria labelled 'the unemployment state'
Gold exploration sector shows strong results: Aurum 155g/t hit, Zenith six-for-six in WA, Kuniko NSW drilling complete
$2.7B in small-cap capital raises flooding the market, testing investor appetite
Data centre energy demand threatens to create an energy supply bust, pressuring AGL, Origin, and power generators
Star's Sydney casino licence remains suspended, weighing on gaming/consumer discretionary
Global AI chip and networking stocks (AMD, Lumentum, Zscaler) show strong momentum, supporting ASX tech sentiment

sectors.trend: Gold exploration names (Aurum, Zenith, Kuniko, Anax Metals, Many Peaks, MinRex) showing strong assay results and drilling progress; however, AUD weakness and falling global risk appetite pressure iron ore and diversified miners
sectors.implications: Gold juniors offer relative outperformance; BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face headwinds from AUD depreciation and softening commodity demand signals

sectors.trend: RBA hawkish stance despite rising unemployment supports net interest margins but raises credit-loss concerns; unemployment surge and renter stress threaten household balance sheets
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX benefit from higher rates short-term but face elevated NPL risk as unemployment climbs; rate pincer limits rate-cut tailwinds

sectors.trend: Data centre boom driving electricity demand but creating supply constraints; energy sector faces structural 'bust' risk as demand outstrips generation capacity
sectors.implications: AGL.AX, AGL, Origin Energy (ORG.AX) and power generators face pricing pressure; renewable and gas names may see demand tailwinds but capex constraints limit supply response

sectors.trend: Largest house price correction in 40 years underway; CBD commercial property under pressure (lending library tower listed at $40m); Dusty Martin selling $20m portfolio
sectors.implications: REITs (VGP.AX, DGL.AX, ICPS.AX) face falling valuations and rising vacancy; residential builders (GRO.AX, MCP.AX) under pressure; defensive positioning warranted

sectors.trend: Renter financial stress, unemployment surge, and rising flight costs squeeze household spending; Star casino licence suspension weighs on gaming; Nike turnaround uncertain
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WBC.AX, and gaming names face soft demand; consumer staples (WOW.AX, COL.AX) offer relative defensiveness

sectors.trend: $2.7B capital raise wave testing market liquidity; global AI chip momentum (AMD, Lumentum, Zscaler) supports sentiment; AI data centre development proceeding without permits signals regulatory gaps
sectors.implications: Micro-X, Arrow Minerals, Mamba showing relative strength; AI/tech exposure via global names positive but ASX-listed tech remains thin

key_themes: RBA rate pincer: hiking into a labour-market deterioration creates a stagflationary risk for equities
AUD depreciation cycle amplifying import inflation and pressuring resource-sector earnings in AUD terms
Property correction of historic magnitude reshaping financials, REITs, and consumer confidence
Gold exploration renaissance in WA and NSW offering small-cap upside
Energy supply-demand imbalance from data centre buildout
Global AI/semiconductor momentum providing a counter-narrative to domestic weakness
Small-cap capital raise flood ($2.7B) diluting shareholder value and testing market depth

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA hiking into rising unemployment (stagflation risk)
risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight financials for NIM benefit; underweight rate-sensitive property and consumer discretionary; hold quality dividend payers
Hedge AUD exposure; favour exporters (BHP.AX, CSL.AX) whose USD revenue offsets AUD weakness; avoid import-heavy consumer names
Reduce REIT and residential builder exposure; monitor bank NPL provisions; favour commercial REITs in CBD with long leases

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Energy supply shortfall from data centre demand
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor AGL.AX, ORG.AX capex guidance; consider gas and renewable infrastructure plays; watch for government intervention
Avoid recent cap-raise names; focus on cash-flow-positive small caps; use ASX 200/300 as core allocation
Underweight consumer discretionary; favour staples (WOW.AX, COL.AX); monitor bank credit-loss provisions

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold exploration juniors with strong assay results
opportunities.rationale: Aurum 155g/t, Zenith six-for-six WA, Kuniko NSW completion signal a gold exploration upcycle; AUD weakness supports gold pricing

opportunities.recommendation: Favour large-cap diversified miners for AUD-hedged earnings
opportunities.rationale: AUD depreciation boosts USD-denominated revenue for BHP, Rio, FMG; quality dividend yield provides downside protection in a falling market

opportunities.recommendation: Selective exposure to global AI/semiconductor leaders via ASX-listed ETFs or direct holdings
opportunities.rationale: AMD, Lumentum, Zscaler showing strong momentum; AI data centre buildout is structural; ASX tech exposure remains thin

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce REIT and residential property exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Largest 40-year house price correction underway; CBD commercial valuations falling; rising unemployment pressures occupancy

defensive_moves.recommendation: Shift toward consumer staples and healthcare for defensive income
defensive_moves.rationale: Renter stress and unemployment surge hit discretionary spending; CSL.AX and WOW.AX offer resilient cash flows and dividends

defensive_moves.recommendation: Avoid recent small-cap capital raises; maintain liquidity buffer
defensive_moves.rationale: $2.7B cap raise wave dilutes shareholders; fourth consecutive ASX losing week signals continued downside risk

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to extend losses in the near term as bond yields climb, AUD weakens, and RBA maintains hawkish bias. Fourth consecutive losing week suggests momentum is firmly negative. Gold juniors and large-cap miners may offer relative outperformance. Expect volatility around RBA communications and unemployment data releases.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook remains cautious. The combination of rising unemployment, a 40-year property correction, and an energy supply squeeze creates a stagflationary backdrop. However, AUD depreciation supports resource exporters, and global AI capex provides a structural growth offset. A RBA pivot to cuts is likely once labour-market deterioration accelerates, providing a medium-term equity catalyst.
key_catalysts: RBA cash rate decision and statement (hawkish hold vs. pivot)
Next unemployment and CPI data releases
AUD/USD trajectory and RBA intervention risk
Iron ore and LNG price trends
Data centre energy demand vs. generation capacity gap
Global AI/semiconductor earnings season (Q3 US results)
Property market bottoming signals (volume, price stabilisation)
watch_list: RBA cash rate and forward guidance
Iron ore (62% Fe) and LNG spot prices
Gold price (XAU/USD) – supports ASX gold juniors
Unemployment rate and renter stress indicators
House price indices (SQM, CoreLogic) – 40-year correction progress
